bio_en: Martin Ter-Galstian, known as Jumshud Gharib, was born in 1882 in the Avlabar quarter of Tiflis and studied at the Nersisian school, which he left at sixteen intending to cross into Ottoman Armenia. As a young operative he executed a traitor at the Koghb salt mine in 1902, was hunted by the tsarist police, sheltered in Baku's oil district and was later tried in Kars as a minor. Sent to Persia by the party in 1904, he crossed the Araxes in September 1907 with Martiros Charukhjian and joined Keri's fighters in the Tabriz revolution. He went on to serve in the World War volunteer movement, never sparing his blood for the Armenian and Persian peoples.
